The evidence is therefore indirect: social spending composition, education/health delivery, mining-related displacement, and conflict-zone service gaps.","evidence":[{"title":"Strengthening Public Social Spending in DRC","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-07-15","url":"https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/227/article-A002-en.xml","summary":"social spending rose and education/health were prioritized, with free primary education expanding access, but social protection remained minimal and much of the budget was still absorbed by salaries and current spending. This is indirect but concrete evidence of non-transparent resource handling rather than neutral distribution.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.5"]},{"title":"Democratic Republic of Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-02-26","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes","summary":"school leaders in Kinshasa and the provinces reported overcrowded classrooms, missing learning materials, weak staffing, and poor water/sanitation, showing the benefits of public spending were still not reaching people evenly.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]}]}
